name: Helblinghaus Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Helblinghaus in Innsbruck's Old Town: a late Gothic burgher house from the 15th century with a world-famous, opulent Rococo stucco facade by Anton Gigl from 1732.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Helblinghaus (located at Herzog-Friedrich-Straße 10) is one of the most outstanding architectural gems in the historic Old Town of Innsbruck. Situated directly opposite the world-famous Golden Roof at the junction with Pfarrgasse, the stately patrician house attracts attention with its spectacular facade. The exuberant, confectionery-like stucco decoration is one of the most perfect and masterful examples of bourgeois Rococo in the entire Alpine region and forms a fascinating contrast to the neighbouring late Gothic buildings.

Route & Requirements

The structural core of the Helblinghaus dates back to the late Gothic period around 1480, when Innsbruck experienced a period of urban prosperity under the Tyrolean territorial princes. Originally built as a typical late Gothic burgher house with oriels and pointed arch passages for wealthy city dwellers, the facade remained simple for centuries. The house owes its current world-famous splendour to the prince-bishop's court cashier Johann Fischer, who acquired the property in 1725. Around 1730 to 1732, Fischer commissioned the Bavarian stucco master Anton Gigl from the famous artist dynasty of the Wessobrunn School to completely redesign the show facade. Gigl covered the entire four-story gable facade and the two polygonal oriels with a dense, filigree network of white stucco marble on a delicate pink background. Floral acanthus tendrils, grapevines, fruit garlands, rocaille, shell forms, mascarons, putti figures, and artfully intertwined strapwork can be discovered. The allegorical reliefs on the oriel balustrades deserve special attention.

Visit & Arrival

The magnificent exterior facade of the Helblinghaus can be viewed and photographed from the outside free of charge at any time of year in the traffic-calmed pedestrian zone of the Old Town. The building is privately owned; traditional retail shops and gastronomic establishments are located on the ground floor, while the upper floors serve as residential units. Arrival by public transport: From Innsbruck main station, it's about a ten-minute walk via Brixner Straße and Maria-Theresien-Straße directly to Herzog-Friedrich-Straße; tram lines 1 and 3 stop at Marktplatz (approx. three minutes' walk away). By car: Park in the Altstadtgarage car park on Innrain or the Markthallengarage.

Tips

The entire pedestrian zone in front of the house is evenly paved and barrier-free for wheelchair users and strollers. The best time of day for detailed shots of the filigree stucco work is in the morning or at lunchtime, when the sunlight particularly plastically highlights the contrast between the white stucco and the pink background. Bring binoculars or a telephoto lens to discover the tiny faces, birds, and grapes in the stucco work.
preis: Free to view from the outside
oeffnungszeiten: Freely accessible from the outside all year round, 24/7
